rounds.text: Prakash Industries is currently trading at a significant discount to its fundamental value, as evidenced by a price-to-book ratio of 0.74x [E2] and a low P/E ratio of 5.97 [E1]. The market is pricing the company for failure, with a reverse DCF analysis indicating that the current share price implies an earnings growth rate of -9.1% [E25]. This pessimism stands in stark contrast to the base case assumption of 10.0% growth, which supports a calculated intrinsic value of Rs 492 per share [E23]. Consequently, the stock offers a substantial margin of safety of 73.8% [E24], a figure reinforced by the scanX signal engine [E38]. Conceded: the stock currently sits at only 24% of its 52-week range, reflecting recent downward pressure [E5]. Despite this market sentiment, the company maintains a solid ROE of 14.1% [E6] and has demonstrated a consistent 10-year compounded share price growth of 13% [E7].

blind_spot_facts.fact: Compounded share price growth over 5 years is 10%.

scorecard.note: Computed arithmetically from the citations that survived grounding — no model input.

evidence.fact: Price-to-book is 0.74x (price ₹ 129 on a book value of ₹ 174).
The stock sits 24% of the way up its 52-week range (110 low to 188 high).
Compounded share price growth over 10 years is 13%.
Compounded share price growth over 5 years is 10%.
A discounted cash flow puts intrinsic value at Rs 492 per share against a market price of Rs 129.
That leaves a margin of safety of 73.8%.
A reverse DCF says today's price already implies -9.1% earnings growth, against the 10.0% the base case assumes.
Screen reason (bull side): DCF margin of safety 74%
